paper_role: direction gate: decides whether the paper stays on cache placement laws (route A) or moves to DiT single-step multi-engine dataflow (route B)
question: Of one real backbone step's wall time on the new trn2.3xlarge node, how much is non-overlapped TensorE (PE) work, how much is exposed collective time, and how much is non-PE engine work (VectorE/ScalarE/GpSimdE/DMA) on the critical path?
why_this_gate: The cache line has no architecture headroom left inside a cached request on this chip (see placement-laws protocol). The only remaining large lever is the anchor step itself, which reaches only ~42% of BF16 peak by FLOP accounting. Whether that gap is recoverable by work placement is an engine-attribution question, not a cache question.

flux.hardware: trn2.3xlarge, one Trainium2 device, 4 logical NeuronCores (LNC=2), 96 GiB HBM
flux.parallelism: TP4, CP1, no CFG-parallel, SP off (the qualified A12 topology)
flux.compiled_root: recorded in the result file (artifact hash), not known before compile

wan.hardware: trn2.3xlarge, one Trainium2 device, 4 logical NeuronCores (LNC=2), 96 GiB HBM
wan.parallelism: TP4 (registry default), serial CFG (two backbone forwards per step)

measurement.compile: difflet compile --model-id <id> --tp-degree 4 --height/--width (--num-frames for Wan); artifact model.pt sha256 recorded in the result
measurement.step_wall: benchmark/step_realloop.py: real denoise loop, inter-step deltas (steps 1..N-1), one generate per model; report P50/P95
measurement.neff_profile: scripts/profile_dit_backbone.py --neff <backbone graph.neff> --world-size 4: neuron-profile summary-json -> per-engine active-time %, MFU/MBU, HBM bytes, DMA active %
measurement.timeline: neuron-profile inspect of one full request; per-core engine/DMA/cc intervals
measurement.attribution: engine-union critical path (CARDAN method): merge each engine's intervals, compute non-overlapped union per engine and exposed cc time (cc_running intervals not covered by any compute-engine interval); dominant engine = largest total AND largest non-overlapped union. Tooling adapted from /home/ubuntu/rd-moe/experiments/engine-breakdown/analyze_frozen_profiles.py and gemma4-decode/scripts/analyze_engine_activity.py
measurement.accounting_window: denoise loop only; text encoders and VAE excluded
measurement.repetitions: 5 profiled steps per model; medians reported; the timeline used for interval metrics is the one whose makespan is closest to the median

pre_estimates.flux_flop_per_step: 74.3 TFLOP (57 blocks x 4608 tokens x 141.5 MMAC x 2)

flux_mfu_pct.basis: 74.3 TFLOP / 0.267 s / 667 TFLOP/s BF16 dense peak = 41.7%

flux_weight_stream_ms_per_step.basis: 11.9 B params x 2 B / 4 cores = 5.95 GB/core at ~0.73 TB/s/core

flux_cc_ops_per_step.basis: 2167 cc ops per request per core over 12 anchors (H1e)

flux_cc_running_ms_per_step.basis: 1215 ms per core per request / 12 anchors (H1e); overlap fraction unknown

flux_non_pe_engine_nonoverlapped_pct.basis: AdaLN modulation, RMSNorm, GELU, RoPE, softmax; no direct prior

pre_estimates.wan: no prior on this node; record only, no prediction scored

decision_rule.metric: X = exposed_cc_pct + non_pe_engine_nonoverlapped_pct, measured on FLUX (primary) and Wan (secondary), median of 5 steps
decision_rule.route_A_cache_laws: X < 20 and TensorE non-overlapped union >= 80% of step -> single-step optimisation headroom <= 1.25x; paper stays on cache placement laws; DiT dataflow is at most an implementation note
decision_rule.route_B_dit_dataflow: X >= 30 on FLUX -> main line becomes DiT single-step multi-engine dataflow (CARDAN method); cache becomes a multiplier and one section
decision_rule.middle: 20 <= X < 30 -> route A main line; the single largest non-PE item becomes one kernel section inside route A
decision_rule.wan_override: if Wan X >= 30 while FLUX X < 20, route B is pursued on Wan only and the paper's DiT section is video-specific
decision_rule.tie_breaker: the rule is evaluated once on the frozen measurement; no re-profiling after the fact to move X across a threshold

not_claimed: This gate produces no speedup claim. Engine-active percentages are occupancy, not FLOP utilisation; the FLOP-based MFU is reported separately.
